claim: Individuals who were neither parties nor privies to consent decrees are not precluded from bringing independent Title VII discrimination claims based on actions taken pursuant to those decrees, and a consent decree entered pursuant to voluntary settlement provides no greater protection against charges of illegal discrimination than a voluntary affirmative action plan.
initial_reasoning: The case at 833 F.2d 1492 expressly holds that plaintiffs who were neither parties nor privies to the consent decrees are not precluded from bringing independent Title VII claims, and it further states that a consent decree entered pursuant to a voluntary settlement affords no greater protection against discrimination claims than a voluntary affirmative action plan.
